replacements.new: For the native RKHS H of a strictly positive kernel, let `V_X=span{K(·,x_i)}` and let `s_X f` be the orthogonal projection of f onto V_X. Define `P_X(x)=||K(·,x)−Π_{V_X}K(·,x)||_H`; the reproducing identity and Cauchy–Schwarz give `|f(x)−s_Xf(x)|≤P_X(x)||f||_H`. The selected native-space branch is one fixed normalized Matérn kernel with arbitrary fixed d≥1, ν>0 and inverse length a>0, spectral density `A(a²+4π²|ξ|²)^(-ν-d/2)` in the negative-sign 2π Fourier convention, where `A=Γ(ν+d/2)(4π)^(d/2)a^(2ν)/Γ(ν)`. On a bounded Lipschitz domain satisfying a uniform interior cone condition, use the standard restriction-quotient Bessel-potential norm for `H^(ν+d/2)(Ω)`. Prove whole-space Fourier/native norm equivalence, restricted-native quotient equivalence, stable polynomial norming stencils from the cone condition, and the Fourier-cutoff domain zeros lemma locally before the rate. The full constructions, foundational supplier interfaces and intermediate ordering are in `research/numerical-analysis-remaining-71-2026-10-17-ROOT-rbf-planning-cycle1/PROOF.md` and its companion REPORT.md. Carry the Choice hypotheses of the actual foundational suppliers as stated there. State fill distance h, separation radius q, mesh ratio ρ=h/q and a small-h threshold. The corresponding `L∞` rate is `C h^ν ||f||_{H^(ν+d/2)(Ω)}`; it holds without a mesh-ratio restriction and hence uniformly under the approved bounded-mesh-ratio hypothesis. Separately prove `λ_min(K_X)≥c q^(2ν)` for q≤1, `λ_max(K_X)≤N`, and the resulting exact-arithmetic condition bounds before discussing separation or numerical solver error. Do not identify the restriction norm with an intrinsic fractional domain norm without supplying that additional theorem. A Gaussian flat-limit stability claim is excluded unless the RBF-QR basis change and its error are separately defined and proved.
